headline: Simulations link cell proliferation, adhesion and polarity to tissue shape patterns
label: Tissue Morphogenesis Simulation Models
summary: Recent preprints couple mechanics, cell-cycle control, and polarity-dependent adhesion to reproduce tissue patterns and pigment self-organization.
synthesis: The dominant thread is mechanistic simulation that links cell-scale rules to tissue-scale spatial organization. Three of the four items model multicellular systems with explicit cell mechanics, proliferation, or adhesion. A cell-cycle model coupled to tissue mechanics, parameterized from Drosophila wing disc time-lapse imaging, reproduces cell area distributions and attributes them to proliferation. A review of Deformable Cell Models, a high-resolution agent-based approach, presents simulation results across in-vitro and tissue settings. A polarity-dependent adhesion model reproduces five embryonic morphogenetic types, with two parameters setting polarity strength and its regulation. The fourth item uses a continuum reaction-diffusion-advection framework with nonlocal Morse-type kernels to simulate how pollutants alter melanophore-xanthophore self-organization in fish pigmentation. What is new is the explicit coupling of proliferation to tissue mechanics and the reduction of polarity-dependent morphogenesis to a small set of controlling parameters, alongside an environmental perturbation treated within the same pattern-formation framework.
